Security-relevant claims the next pass should check against real source, since the changelog is only a description: (1) Request normalization v8 to v9 changes prompt_contract_id. Per the changelog, a coordinator attaches a cache scope only when the provider's contract matches, so a mismatch fails toward no prefix-cache reuse, which is conservative for T-041 cross-account isolation. Source should confirm that the cacheSalt/scope derivation (coordinator/registry/cache_route_keys.go and the CBv2Request.cacheSalt plumbing) still binds account, model build and prompt contract. (2) Nemotron Super prefix reuse is described as 'partitioned by the authenticated cache scope', and the image path reuses only checkpoints bound to the same image features. This should be verified against T-041 (a). (3) The GLM encrypted SSD prefix store is described as default-on for the pinned GLM identity, with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the opt-out. This extends the at-rest surface under T-041/SEC-035 to another model, so the TTL, HMAC lookup and per-donation gating should be confirmed unchanged. (4) Weight hashing and shard loading 'read around the file cache'; the verification semantics (T-012, T-027) should be confirmed unchanged. (5) New media ingress paths (PNG/JPEG/MP4 decoding, AVFoundation, inline video) carry bounds and in-memory handling claims; they should be checked against T-050 for no plaintext temp files. (6) The MLX, mlx-swift and mlx-swift-lm pin bumps change kernels and are not reviewable here. (7) Cancellation, 429/503 and wedged-slot retirement claims relate to T-010 and availability. The unit is a patch with the 'Upgrade and rollout notes' and rollback env switches, but 'darkbloom start' not forwarding them to the LaunchAgent is a documented limitation, not a finding. No threat-model assumption is contradicted by the supplied text; the coverage limit is that the underlying code is not supplied.
